arxiv-2202-08072.title: Accurate measures of regional lung air volumes from chest x-rays of small animals
arxiv-2202-08072.creator: D. W. O’Connell, K. S. Morgan, G. Ruben, L. C.P. Croton, J. A. Pollock, M. K. Croughan, E. V. McGillick, M. J. Wallace, K. J. Crossley, E. J. Pryor, R. A. Lewis, S. B. Hooper, M. J. Kitchen
arxiv-2202-08072.description: Abstract We present a robust technique for calculating regional volume changes within the lung from X-ray radiograph sequences captured during ventilation, without the use of computed tomography (CT). This technique is based on the change in transmitted X-ray intensity that occurs for each lung region as air displaces the attenuating lung tissue.

arxiv-2303-03600.title: Adaptive Knowledge Distillation between Text and Speech Pre-trained Models
arxiv-2303-03600.creator: Jinjie Ni 1,2,∗ , Yukun Ma 1 , Wen Wang 1 , Qian Chen 1 , Dianwen Ng 1,2 , Han Lei 2 , Trung Hieu Nguyen 1 , Chong Zhang 1 , Bin Ma 1 , Erik Cambria 2
arxiv-2303-03600.description: Abstract Learning on a massive amount of speech corpus leads to the recent success of many self-supervised speech models. With knowledge distillation, these models may also benefit from the knowledge encoded by language models that are pre-trained on rich sources of texts. The distillation process, however, is challenging due to the modal disparity between textual and speech embedding spaces.

arxiv-2307-00209.title: Image Matters: A New Dataset and Empirical Study for Multimodal Hyperbole Detection
arxiv-2307-00209.description: Abstract Hyperbole, or exaggeration, is a common linguistic phenomenon. The detection of hyperbole is an important part of understanding human expression. There have been several studies on hyperbole detection, but most of which focus on text modality only. However, with the development of social media, people can create hyperbolic expressions with various modalities, including text, images, videos, etc.

arxiv-2311-12298.title: Noise in Relation Classification Dataset TACRED: Characterization and Reduction
arxiv-2311-12298.creator: Akshay Parekh, Ashish Anand and Amit Awekar
arxiv-2311-12298.description: Abstract . TACRED, a large-scale crowd-sourced supervised dataset for Relation Classification, has already been shown noisy by earlier studies. A significant performance improvement was observed when instances with label noise were manually reannotated with the help of linguistic experts or crowd-sourcing with improved guidelines. However, the nature of noise in the dataset is largely unexplored.

arxiv-2501-03271.title: Thanks: Work done outside of role at Meta. Thanks: Work done outside of role at Amazon.
arxiv-2501-03271.creator: Amitava Das 1, Suranjana Trivedy 1, Danush Khanna 1, Rajarshi Roy 1, Gurpreet Singh 1
arxiv-2501-03271.description: Abstract The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) has revolutionized numerous applications, but presents significant challenges in aligning these models with diverse human values, ethical standards, and specific user preferences. Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has become a cornerstone for preference alignment but is constrained by reliance on fixed divergence measures and limited feature transformations.

arxiv-2503-20007.title: Low-resource Machine Translation for Code-switched Kazakh-Russian Language Pair
arxiv-2503-20007.creator: Maksim Borisov, Zhanibek Kozhirbayev, Valentin Malykh
arxiv-2503-20007.description: Abstract Аннотация Machine translation for low resource language pairs is a challenging task. This task could become extremely difficult once a speaker uses code switching. We propose a method to build a machine translation model for code-switched Kazakh-Russian language pair with no labeled data. Our method is basing on generation of synthetic data.

arxiv-2601-20958.title: First constraints on causal sources of primordial gravitational waves from BICEP/Keck, SPTpol, SPT-3G, Planck and WMAP B B -mode data
arxiv-2601-20958.creator: Jessica A. Zebrowski, Aurora Ireland, Christian L. Reichardt, Kylar Greene, Gordan Krnjaic, Yuhsin Tsai, François R Bouchet
arxiv-2601-20958.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Jessica A. Zebrowski, Aurora Ireland, Christian L. Reichardt, Kylar Greene, Gordan Krnjaic, Yuhsin Tsai, François R Bouchet. Non-inflationary sources of gravitational waves in the early Universe generically predict causality-limited tensor power spectra at low frequencies. We report the first-ever constraints on such sources based on cosmic microwave background (CMB) B B -mode polarization measurements.

pmc-10689107.title: Multiple Gestation as a Risk Factor for SARS-CoV-2-Associated Adverse Maternal Outcome: Data From the COVID-19 Related Obstetric and Neonatal Outcome Study (CRONOS)
pmc-10689107.creator: Marina Sourouni, Ariane Germeyer, Manuel Feißt, Alexandra Balzer, Helen Köster, Annemarie Minte, Dörthe Brüggmann, Celine Kohll, Kristin Reinhardt, Michaela Möginger, Anja Leonhardt, Constanze Banz-Jansen, Michael Bohlmann, Christiane Fröhlich, Clara Backes, Dietrich Hager, Lisa Kaup, Elsa Hollatz-G
pmc-10689107.description: IntroductionStudies have shown that pregnant women with COVID-19 have a higher risk of intensive care unit admission and invasive mechanical ventilation support than non-pregnant women. Pregnancy-associated physiological changes in respiratory function may contribute to the elevated risk. Alteration in lung volumes and capacities are attributed to the mechanical impediment caused by the growing fetus.

pmc-10770690.title: Immunohistochemical Study of the Expressed Cluster Differentiation Markers Proteins Type 20 And 56 in Breast Tissues from a Group of Iraqi Patients with Breast Cancers
pmc-10770690.creator: Sarmad M H Zeiny, Saad Hasan Mohammed Ali
pmc-10770690.description: Background:Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) are important immunological components in response to cancers. Patients with higher numbers of TIL in breast cancerous tissues, comprising T- cytotoxic and T – helper cells along with B- and rare natural killer (NK) cells, have more favorable clinical outcomes.

pmc-11342269.title: Francisella novicida infection in a patient with pulmonary infection and pancreatitis in Italy
pmc-11342269.creator: Sara Rigamonti, Emanuela Olivieri, Nadia Vicari, Erika Scaltriti, Moira Bazzucchi, Claudio Marco Lodola, Arianna Torri, Vittorio Sambri, Carlo Biagetti, Paola Prati
pmc-11342269.description: Tularemia is a rare but potentially life threatening zoonotic disease caused by Francisella tularensis. F. novicida, previously considered a subspecies of F. tularensis, is currently considered a separate species. Human infections related to F. novicida are exceedingly rare but can cause morbidity and mortality in debilitated or immunocompromised individuals.

pmc-11509756.title: Quantitative Evaluation of Microcirculatory Alterations in Patients with COVID-19 and Bacterial Septic Shock through Remote Photoplethysmography and Automated Capillary Refill Time Analysis
pmc-11509756.creator: Mara Klibus, Darja Smirnova, Zbignevs Marcinkevics, Uldis Rubins, Andris Grabovskis, Indulis Vanags, Olegs Sabelnikovs, Nicoleta Alice Dragoescu
pmc-11509756.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and Objectives: Sepsis, a leading global health challenge, accounts for around 20% of deaths worldwide. The complexity of sepsis, especially the difference between bacterial and viral etiologies, requires an effective assessment of microcirculation during resuscitation. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of infusion therapy on microcirculation in patients with sepsis, focusing on bacterial- and COVID-19-associated sepsis using remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) and the automated capillary refill time (aCRT).

pmc-11704616.title: High-throughput specificity profiling of antibody libraries using ribosome display and microfluidics
pmc-11704616.creator: Ellen K. Wagner, Kyle P. Carter, Yoong Wearn Lim, Geeyun Jenny Chau, Alexis Enstrom, Nicholas P. Wayham, Jessica-Mae Hanners, Chiann-Ling C. Yeh, Marc Fouet, Jackson Leong, Adam S. Adler, Jan Fredrik Simons
pmc-11704616.description: SummaryIn this work, we developed PolyMap (polyclonal mapping), a high-throughput method for mapping protein-protein interactions. We demonstrated the mapping of thousands of antigen-antibody interactions between diverse antibody libraries isolated from convalescent and vaccinated COVID-19 donors and a set of clinically relevant SARS-CoV-2 spike variants.

pmc-12388286.title: Health-Related QoL of Hypertensive Patients in Bulgaria—Population-Based, Regional Pilot Study
pmc-12388286.creator: Zornitsa Mitkova, Elena Dimitrova, Hristiana Tomova, Nikolay Gerasimov, Diyan Gospodinov, Konstantin Mitov, Stamen Pishev, Boryana Parashkevova, Guenka Petrova
pmc-12388286.description: Background and Objectives: The goal of this study is to assess health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using the EuroQoL (EQ-5D-5L) and identify factors that might contribute to it. Materials and Methods: This is a real-life, observational study involving 234 hypertensive patients from Sofia and Burgas, conducted between January 2024 and July 2024.

pmc-12411731.title: Sedative and echocardiographic effects of intranasal or intramuscular administration of dexmedetomidine in healthy cats
pmc-12411731.creator: Zhaoyi Liu, Huan Yang, Shuai Li, Jiayi Tian, Zhen Yang, Xinyi Xu, Meng Li
pmc-12411731.description: ObjectivesThe aim of the present study was to evaluate the sedative and echocardiographic effects of dexmedetomidine (DEX) administered via intranasal (IN) and intramuscular (IM) routes in cats.MethodsThis randomised, blinded crossover study involved eight healthy adult cats. Cats were randomly allocated to receive DEX 10 μg/kg via either the IN or IM routes.

pmc-13182603.title: Terminal loop sequences in viral double-stranded RNAs modulate RIG-I signaling
pmc-13182603.creator: Matthew Hackbart, Patrick Wang, Victoria Gnazzo, Carolina B López
pmc-13182603.description: Detection of foreign RNAs is a crucial activation step for innate immunity pathways in response to viral infections. Retinoic acid–inducible gene I (RIG-I) is a cytoplasmic RNA sensor that triggers type I and III interferon (IFN) expression and activates the antiviral response during RNA virus infections.
